'''Carol Ann Beaumont'''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.parliament.nz/en-NZ/PB/Debates/Debates/5/c/4/49HansD_20081208_00000010-Members-Sworn.htm|title=New Zealand Hansard - Members Sworn [Volume:651;Page:2]|publisher=[[New Zealand Parliament]]|accessdate=2017-03-15}}</ref> {{post-nominals|country=NZL|ONZM|size=85%}} (born 6 October 1960) is a New Zealand unionist and Labour Party politician. She twice served as a list member of Parliament from 2008 to 2011 and 2013 to 2014, and was elected Labour Party senior vice president in 2021.<ref name=":0" />

==Early life and career==
Beaumont worked for several unions before entering Parliament, including the [[New Zealand Union of Students' Associations|New Zealand University Students' Association]], New Zealand Nurses Association and [[New Zealand Council of Trade Unions]] (NZCTU).<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Beaumont, Carol - New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/former-members-of-parliament/beaumont-carol/ |access-date=2022-08-29 |website=www.parliament.nz |language=en}}</ref> She was NZCTU Secretary from 2003 until 2008.<ref name="Department of Labour">{{cite web |title=Carol Beaumont |url=http://www.dol.govt.nz/services/PartnershipResourceCentre/Carol-Beaumont-Advisory-Board.asp |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081015114613/http://dol.govt.nz/services/PartnershipResourceCentre/Carol-Beaumont-Advisory-Board.asp |archivedate=15 October 2008 |accessdate=2008-12-11 |publisher=[[Department of Labour (New Zealand)|Department of Labour]]}}</ref>

== Political career ==

Beaumont stood for Labour at the [[2008 New Zealand general election|2008 general election]] in [[Maungakiekie (New Zealand electorate)|Maungakiekie]], an electorate that was held at the time by the retiring  [[Mark Gosche]]. She finished second to Auckland City councillor [[Sam Lotu-Iiga]], the National Party candidate.<ref>{{cite web |date=2008-11-22 |title=Official Count Results - Maungakiekie |url=http://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2008/electorate-25.html |accessdate=2017-03-15 |website=Electionresults.govt.nz}}</ref> Beaumont was elected to Parliament as a list MP. Labour was in opposition and Beaumont was appointed Labour spokesperson for consumer affairs and associate spokesperson for labour. In early 2010 she took over responsibility for [[Charles Chauvel (politician)|Charles Chauvel]]'s Credit Reforms (Responsible Lending) Bill, which had been drawn from the ballot in August 2009.<ref>{{cite web |date=21 July 2010 |title=Credit Reforms (Responsible Lending) Bill |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/bills-and-laws/bills-digests/document/49PLLawBD17841/credit-reforms-responsible-lending-bill-2010-bills-digest/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210520195223/https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/bills-and-laws/bills-digests/document/49PLLawBD17841/credit-reforms-responsible-lending-bill-2010-bills-digest/ |archive-date=20 May 2021 |access-date=20 May 2021 |website=www.parliament.nz |publisher=Parliament of New Zealand}}</ref> The bill was defeated at its first reading in July 2010.<ref>{{cite web |date=2010-07-21 |title=Loan sharks "not going away" |url=http://tvnz.co.nz/politics-news/loan-shark-bill-killed-first-reading-3665374 |accessdate=2010-07-22 |publisher=[[TVNZ]]}}</ref>[[File:Mining Protest-4 cropped.jpg|thumb|left|Beaumont (right), with [[Jacinda Ardern]] and [[Phil Goff]]]]
At the [[2011 New Zealand general election|2011 general election]] Beaumont again finished second to Lotu-Iiga in [[Maungakiekie (New Zealand electorate)|Maungakiekie]]. Despite a higher list rating than in 2008, Labour did not poll high enough for Beaumont to be returned as a list MP until the 2013 resignation of Charles Chauvel. In her second term, Beaumont was Labour spokesperson for women's affairs and consumer rights and standards.<ref name=":1" />

At the [[2014 New Zealand general election|2014 election]] Beaumont contested {{NZ electorate link|Maungakiekie}} a third time. Boundary changes were assumed to make the seat safer for Labour,<ref>{{cite web |title= Sam Lotu IIga Claims Maungakiekie |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/10524978/Sam-Lotu-Iiga-claims-Maungakiekie |publisher=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |accessdate= 31 January 2015 }}</ref> but Beaumont was defeated by Lotu-Iiga for a third time and was not re-elected on the party list. She did not contest the 2017 election.

===Post-parliamentary career===
In 2021 Beaumont was elected vice-president of the Labour Party following the resignation of [[Tracey McLellan]], who had been elected to parliament the previous year.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=Party Information | url=https://www.labour.org.nz/party_info |website=[[New Zealand Labour Party]] |accessdate=8 May 2021 }}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
[[File:Carol Beaumont ONZM investiture.jpg|thumb|right|Beaumont (right), after her investiture as an [[Officer of the New Zealand Order of Merit]] by the governor-general, [[Cindy Kiro|Dame Cindy Kiro]], at [[Government House, Auckland]], on 27 May 2022]]
In the [[2021 Birthday Honours (New Zealand)|2021 Queen's Birthday Honours]], Beaumont was appointed an [[Officer of the New Zealand Order of Merit]], for services to the union movement and women's rights.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dpmc.govt.nz/publications/queens-birthday-honours-list-2021 |title=Queen's Birthday honours list 2021 |date=7 June 2021 |publisher=Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet |access-date=7 June 2021}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Beaumont's partner, Robert Gallagher, was one of the [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour Party]] campaign team strategists and in January 2015 announced his intention to stand for the [[New Zealand Labour Party#List of presidents|Labour Party Presidency]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nominees announced for Labour Party presidency |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11392042 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] | date=23 January 2015 |accessdate= 31 January 2015 }}</ref> He was unsuccessful.
